newsitem.title: UK: European shares hit peaks, Wall St leads way.
newsitem.headline: European shares hit peaks, Wall St leads way.

text.p: Stock markets struck records across Europe on Thursday, boosted by fresh gains on Wall Street, but the dollar stalled as investors pondered the chances of central banks intervening to halt its rise.

London, German and French shares closed at historic highs after Wall Street continued Wednesday's blistering performance that saw the Dow Industrial Average come tantalisingly within sight of 7,000 points.
The Dow clawed its way to an inter-day high of 6,995 but was unable to make the final leap through 7,000 points before European markets closed.
Its performance was enough to drag the Belgian, Norwegian and Danish stock markets to fresh highs, too.
Foreign exchange markets were dominated by worries that the central banks of the main industrialised countries could intervene to cap the dollar's surge.

An attempt to push the dollar to a new 34-month high at 1.6935 marks was thwarted by the vice-president of the German Bundesbank, Johann Wilhelm Gaddum, who reiterated the central bank line that it was not in its interests to have the dollar rising "further and further."
While this added some jitters about what would happen if the dollar gained further ground, analysts said that it was only likely to create a minor delay before the currency moved higher.

"While day traders are understandably a little worried about the threat of intervention, longer-term players are not being scared as easily becuase the don't belive either Germnay or Japan will back it up with interest rate increases," said Paul Meggyesi, currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
The dollar largely ignored U.S. retail sales figures, which showed a 0.6 percent rise in January, slightly less than forecasts of a 0.7 percent gain.
By 1700 GMT the dollar was holding its own at 1.6865 marks and 124.32 yen compared with 1.6820 marks and 123.81 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.

European bond markets kicked off the day in a chirpy mood, but British government gilts retreated after political and inflation worries dogged the market. In contrast, German bund futures closed just below an all-time high set during the morning..
Wall Street's overnight gains, propelled by the strength of the dollar and powerful inflows into U.S. mutual funds, set the tone for Asian and European stock markets.

German shares continued their record-setting advance with the 30-share DAX index hitting a fresh closing high of 3,229.48 points in floor trade. In later screen-based trading the IBIS DAX echoed the bourse performance, closing at a record 3,256.86 for a rise of 1.43 percent.
"We're following the dollar and the Dow this afternoon. Liquidity is pouring in and 3,300 points could be the next big event for the DAX," a Frankfurt trader said.
"People don't know what's hit them with this bull run, but no-one wants to go against it -- everyone wants to enjoy this while it lasts," another said.

Analysts said the key to the current run is the rise of the dollar, which helped make cars one of the best performing sectors. Volkswagen AG shares were up 8.30 marks at 820 marks in afternoon IBIS trade.
French shares closed at a record high after a 1.2 percent jump that was underpinned by the rising dollar and Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.08 points at 2,628.41 after hitting an intra-day high of 2,631.89.

Bouygues dropped 5.15 percent to 553 francs and Generale des Eaux set an all-time high of 802 francs after railway company SNCF selected Generale of the two to operate its nationwide fibre optic telecoms network.

Europe's largest stock market, London, rose strongly to close at a record high of 4,327.1, easily surpassing the previous closing peak of 4,307.8 set on February 7. The FTSE 100 earlier came to a halt just shy of its all-time high of 4,330.
Retail inflation data showed price rises slightly higher than expected but analysts said a near-term interest rate rise was still extremely unlikely and the FTSE ignored the news.
"The data today suggests that the economy is doing nothing other than growing above trend," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
Dealers said sentiment was underpinned by encouraging annual results from Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc and news of a possible bid approach for Chubb Security .
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6865 marks and 124.32 yen compared with 1.6820 marks and 123.81 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 22.8 points, or 0.53 percent, at 4,327.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 29.08 points, or 1.12 percent, at 2,628.41.

FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 13.34 points, or 0.41 percent, at a record 3,229.48. In later screen-based trade the the IBIS DAX index ended up 45.85 points, or 1.43 percent, to 3,256.86.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $341.85, up 70 cents. Silver finished up 24 cents at $5.14.
